references.text: Moses explains that the Lord did not choose Israel because of their greatness, but because of His love and the promise He gave to the fathers.
The preceding verse warns Israel against believing that their righteousness is the reason they receive the land.
Moses emphasizes again that it is not because of Israel's righteousness, for they are a stiff-necked people.
God tells Abraham that the sin of the Amorites is not yet full, pointing to the wickedness of the nations as the reason for their expulsion.
The Lord's promise to Abraham to give the land to his offspring.
God confirms His promise to Isaac to give him and his offspring these lands.
God repeats His promise to Jacob regarding the land and a great offspring.
The sin and uncleanness of the nations as the reason the land spewed them out.
Paul explains that God's election is not based on works, but on His calling and grace.
Salvation is by grace, not by works; otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
Salvation is a gift from God, not of works, so that no one may boast.
God saved us not because of our righteous deeds, but according to His mercy.
